summary.text: List 2 of River's Spelling Bee study words: sniffling, beneath, tractor, permit, awning, fickle, relief, lunar, boycotting, molten, elite, woven, proclaim.

why.text: This is the real Scripps "Two Bee" fourth-grade word list — the words a school spelling bee actually draws from. Saying each word aloud, letter by letter, is the same skill a real bee tests, not just recognizing the word on a page.

objectives.text: Spell every word on this list correctly, letter by letter, from hearing it alone.
State each word's meaning in your own words.

parentNote.text: Built from "Spelling Bee Words", the 2026-27 Scripps Two Bee fourth-grade study list you added to her Drive folder. All 50 official words are split across four lessons; every definition and example sentence here was written fresh, since the source is a bare word list with no definitions to copy. The flashcards use the honeycomb "bee" look, and each lesson also opens the Spelling Bee voice game — hear it, spell it aloud letter by letter.

nextUp.text: Cards first to learn the meanings, then the Spelling Bee game to practice saying the letters aloud.

cards.def:
**Breathing in short, audible sniffs through the nose, often from crying or a cold.**
• He came in sniffling and wiping his nose after the walk in the rain.

**In or to a lower position than something else; underneath.**
• The cat curled up beneath the porch to stay cool.
cards.hint: BE- + NEATH — "neath" is an old word for "under" on its own.

cards.def:
**A powerful vehicle with large wheels, used to pull farm machinery or heavy loads.**
• The farmer drove the tractor slowly along the fence line.

**To allow something to happen, or an official paper that gives permission for something.**
• You need a permit to build a fence that tall.

**A rooflike cover, often made of canvas or metal, that extends over a window, door, or patio.**
• Rain drummed steadily on the striped awning above the café tables.
cards.hint: AWN- + -ING — do not forget the N before -ing.

cards.def:
**Likely to change opinions, loyalty, or feelings suddenly and without warning.**
• The weather this week has been fickle — sun one hour, rain the next.

**A feeling of comfort or reassurance after worry, pain, or difficulty ends.**
• Finding her lost keys brought a wave of relief.
cards.hint: "I" before "E" except after "C" — so it is L-I-E-F.

cards.def:
**Relating to or connected with the moon.**
• A lunar eclipse happens when Earth's shadow falls across the moon.
cards.hint: LUN- (like "lunatic", which the Romans blamed on the moon) + -AR.

cards.def:
**Refusing to buy, use, or take part in something, as a form of organized protest.**
• The neighborhood was boycotting the store until it lowered its prices.

**Melted by great heat, especially describing rock or metal in liquid form.**
• Molten lava glowed orange as it flowed down the volcano's side.
cards.hint: MOLT- + -EN, like "melt" with a different vowel.

cards.def:
**A select, small group of people considered the best, most skilled, or most powerful in their field.**
• Only the elite runners qualified for the final race.
cards.hint: One L, then -LITE, like "light" without the GH.

cards.def:
**Formed by crossing threads or strips over and under one another, as cloth or a basket is made.**
• The basket was woven from thin strips of willow.

**To announce something officially and publicly, often with importance or authority.**
• The mayor stood on the steps to proclaim the city's new holiday.
cards.hint: PRO- + CLAIM — "claim" hides right inside it.

questions.q: Spell the word: breathing in short, audible sniffs through the nose, often from crying or a cold.
steps: Drop the final F is wrong — keep both Fs.

ex.tip: "Sniff" keeps its double F all the way through, even with -ling attached.

questions.q: Spell the word: in or to a lower position than something else; underneath.
questions.hint: BE- + NEATH — "neath" is an old word for "under" on its own.
steps: The EA says a long E sound, like in "each".

questions.q: Spell the word: a powerful vehicle with large wheels, used to pull farm machinery or heavy loads.

ex.tip: It ends in -OR like "actor" and "doctor", not -ER.

questions.q: Spell the word: to allow something to happen, or an official paper that gives permission for something.
steps: One T at the end, not two.

ex.tip: Related to "permission" and "permissible" — all share the same PER-M- start.

questions.q: Spell the word: a rooflike cover, often made of canvas or metal, that extends over a window, door, or patio.
questions.hint: AWN- + -ING — do not forget the N before -ing.
steps: A-W-N, three letters before the ending.

ex.tip: It is easy to drop the N by accident — say "awn" slowly to hear it.

questions.q: Spell the word: likely to change opinions, loyalty, or feelings suddenly and without warning.

ex.tip: Rhyme it with "pickle" and the CK-LE pattern falls into place.

questions.q: Spell the word: a feeling of comfort or reassurance after worry, pain, or difficulty ends.
questions.hint: "I" before "E" except after "C" — so it is L-I-E-F.

ex.tip: No C anywhere in this word, so the ordinary I-before-E rule applies with no exception.

questions.q: Spell the word: relating to or connected with the moon.
questions.hint: LUN- (like "lunatic", which the Romans blamed on the moon) + -AR.

ex.tip: It ends in -AR, matching "solar" — its opposite for the sun.

questions.q: Spell the word: refusing to buy, use, or take part in something, as a form of organized protest.
steps: Double T stays before the ending.

ex.tip: "Boycott" already ends in double T on its own — -ing does not add a third.

questions.q: Spell the word: melted by great heat, especially describing rock or metal in liquid form.
questions.hint: MOLT- + -EN, like "melt" with a different vowel.
steps: M-O-L-T, an O not an E.

ex.tip: It looks like "melt" but the vowel changes to O — say it slowly to hear the difference.

questions.q: Spell the word: a select, small group of people considered the best, most skilled, or most powerful in their field.
questions.hint: One L, then -LITE, like "light" without the GH.
steps: L-I-T-E — one L, silent E at the end.

ex.tip: Just one L in the middle — doubling it is the most common slip.

questions.q: Spell the word: formed by crossing threads or strips over and under one another, as cloth or a basket is made.

ex.tip: "Weave" becomes "wove" in the past tense, and "woven" just adds N to that.

questions.q: Spell the word: to announce something officially and publicly, often with importance or authority.
questions.hint: PRO- + CLAIM — "claim" hides right inside it.
steps: "Claim" spells exactly as you already know it: C-L-A-I-M.

ex.tip: If you can spell "claim", you already know the second half of this word.
